<Aside type="caution" title="Update: Next is retired — the old `next build` framing is obsolete">
This page was written when `next build` was the operator's real
typechecker. **Next.js is now retired** — `apps/operator` has no
`next build`, no `next.config.js`, and no `.next-prod/types/*`. The
operator builds via Vite (`@papercusp/operator-vite`'s `vite build`),
which does **not** typecheck by default, so there is no single "real
typechecker reports zero" oracle anymore. What survives unchanged: bare
`tsc --noEmit` against `apps/operator/` reports a large **pre-existing
baseline** (re-measured at ~379 on 2026-06-08, down from the ~860 below;
the count drifts as the tree changes), `--ignoreDeprecations 6.0` is
still required, and the right move is still to **scope your check to the
files you touched**, not the total. The per-file recipe below still works.
</Aside>

## What

Running `tsc --noEmit` directly against `apps/operator/` reports
**hundreds of errors** on a clean checkout (~379 as of 2026-06-08;
historically ~860). These are a real, persistent pre-existing baseline —
`tsc` is not finding regressions, it's the accumulated debt of a tree
that is built/bundled (Vite) rather than typecheck-gated.

The error count fluctuates as other agents land changes —
don't treat a small delta as a regression in either direction. Establish
the baseline, then check only your touched files against it.

## How to verify your work

Always run `tsc` from `apps/operator/`, but **scope your check to the
files you touched**, not the total:

```bash
cd /home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup/apps/operator && \
  ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --ignoreDeprecations 6.0 2>&1 | \
  tee /tmp/tsc.log | grep -cE 'error TS'   # capture baseline

# Then per-file:
for f in path/to/your/file1.tsx path/to/your/file2.ts; do
  n=$(grep -cE "^${f//\//\\/}\(" /tmp/tsc.log)
  printf "  %4d  %s\n" "$n" "$f"
done
```

A clean PR has **zero errors in touched files**, regardless of
project total. The flags matter: `--ignoreDeprecations 6.0` is
required because the repo's `tsconfig.json` uses options newer `tsc`
versions deprecated.

## If you must chase the baseline

Don't. Bare `tsc` is a fast-but-noisy file-level check, not a
project-correctness signal — and since Next's typecheck-on-build is
gone, there is no build step that will independently "report zero" to
chase toward. Verify behavior by running the app via the Tauri dev
shell (`cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`) and by the affected test
suites (`npm run test:affected`), and confirm only that your touched
files are `tsc`-clean against the baseline.

## Why this was costly

This session, I twice spent meaningful time investigating "new"
errors in `lib/agent-tools/plans/*` that turned out to be the pre-
existing baseline. Stashing the diff and re-running `tsc` confirmed
they were already there. The diagnosis loop is fast (1–2 minutes
with `git stash push -u <files>` + re-run) but it shouldn't be
necessary — knowing the baseline exists short-circuits the chase.
